source.title: Twenty Open Problems in Enumeration of Matchings: Progress Report

accepted.question_text: Determine the number of rhombus tilings of a hexagon with side lengths (a, b+1, c, a+1, b, c+1) after the central triangle has been removed.

evidence.quote: Problem 2: Christian Krattenthaler and Soichi Okada have evaluated the number of rhombus tilings of an (a, b + 1, c, a + 1, b, c + 1)-hexagon with the central triangle removed

accepted.question_text: Determine the number of rhombus tilings of a hexagon with side lengths a, b+3, c, a+3, b, c+3 when one arbitrary triangular region is removed from each of the three longer sides.
accepted.context_brief: Hexagon with three missing border triangles

evidence.quote: Problem 3: Theresia Eisenkölbl solved this problem. What she does in fact is to compute the number of all rhombus tilings of a hexagon with sides a, b+3, c, a+3, b, c+3 where an arbitrary triangle is removed from each of the "long" sides of the hexagon

accepted.question_text: Determine the number of rhombus tilings of a hexagon with side lengths a, b, a, a, b, a, where a and b have the same parity, that contain the rhombus touching the center of the hexagon and lying on the symmetry axis parallel to the sides of length b.
accepted.context_brief: Symmetric hexagon with fixed central-axis rhombus

evidence.quote: Fulmek and Krattenthaler compute the number of rhombus tilings of a hexagon with sides a, b, a, a, b, a (with a and b having the same parity) that contain the rhombus touching the center of the hexagon and lying symmetric with respect to the symmetry axis that runs parallel to the sides of length b.

accepted.question_text: For each positive integer n, does the number of perfect matchings of the n-dimensional cube have the same parity as n?
accepted.context_brief: Parity of perfect matchings in the n-cube

evidence.quote: Problem 19: Laszlo Lovasz gave a simple proof of my (oral) conjecture that the number of perfect matchings of the n-cube has the same parity as n itself.

accepted.question_text: Let f(n) denote the number of perfect matchings of the n-dimensional cube. Determine the sequence f(n) modulo 2^m for arbitrary positive integers m.

evidence.quote: The claim follows, and similar albeit more complex reasoning should allow one to compute the enumerating sequence modulo any power of 2.
Meanwhile, L.H. Clark, J.C. George, and T.D. Porter ... show that if one lets f(n) denote the number of 1-factors in the n-cube

needs_review.question_text_raw: One might still try to look for a proof whose simplicity is comparable to that of the answer "one-third".

evidence.quote: One might still try to look for a proof whose simplicity is comparable to that of the answer "one-third".
the special case a = 2n − 1, b = 2n solves Problem 1

evidence.quote: Problem 8: Harald Helfgott has solved this problem.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Problem 9: This was already solved when I posed the problem; it is a special case of Theorem 4.1 in Ciucu's paper "Enumeration of perfect matchings in graphs with reflective symmetry".

evidence.quote: Problem 9: This was already solved when I posed the problem; it is a special case of Theorem 4.1 in Ciucu's paper "Enumeration of perfect matchings in graphs with reflective symmetry"

needs_review.question_text_raw: Problem 10 was solved independently three times, but the exact special-case statement of Problem 10 is not restated in this source.

evidence.quote: Problem 10: This problem was solved independently three times: by Harald Helfgott and Ira Gessel, by Christian Krattenthaler, and by Eric Kuo.
it gives several results concerning the enumeration of perfect matchings of Aztec rectangles where (a suitable number of) collinear vertices are removed, of which Problem 10 is just a special case.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Problem 14 concerns domino tilings of the Aztec window of inner order x and outer order x+w, but the source does not define "Aztec window" or state the original target assertion precisely enough for a standalone rewrite.

evidence.quote: Problem 14: Constantin Chiscanu found a polynomial bound on the number of domino tilings of the Aztec window of inner order x and outer order x + w
Doug Zare used the transfer-matrix method to show that the number of tilings is not just bounded by a polynomial, but given by a polynomial, for each fixed w

trace.notes: Resolved the original zbMATH URL to the exact arXiv work math/9801061 and downloaded the 4-page PDF used for extraction. The document is a progress report organized as short status updates for numbered problems rather than a full restatement of every original problem.
Accepted Problem 2 because the source explicitly states the underlying counting question and marks it as evaluated.
Accepted Problem 3 because the source restates the generalized tiling-count question in enough detail for a standalone rewrite.
Accepted the second part of Problem 4 because the source explicitly describes the tiling configuration that was solved.
Accepted the parity conjecture from Problem 19 because the full conjectural statement is visible in the source and its solved status is explicit.
Accepted the modulo-2^m extension from Problem 19 as an explicit remaining direction tied to the enumerating sequence f(n).
Moved Problem 1 to needs_review because the source only mentions a simpler proof for the answer "one-third" without restating the underlying problem in a self-contained way.
Moved Problem 8 to needs_review because the source reports only that it was solved and does not restate the question.
Moved Problem 9 to needs_review because the source identifies it only as a special case of an external theorem and does not expose the original statement.
Moved Problem 10 to needs_review because the source describes surrounding general results but not the exact special-case statement of Problem 10 itself.

Moved Problem 14 to needs_review because the phrase "Aztec window" is source-specific terminology left undefined in this short progress report, so a standalone rewrite would require unsupported background.
Moved Problem 15 to needs_review because the source gives only a solved-status update without the question text.
Moved Problem 16 to needs_review because the source gives only a solved-status update without the question text.
Moved Problem 18 to needs_review because the source points to an external response and does not present the problem statement or response content in the chosen artifact.
Saved JSON to outputs/parse-paper/math-9801061.json and outputs/latest.json.
